notIncluded.label: Registered agent service
notIncluded.reason: Only if you hire a registered agent. The agent sets the price, so it is not a state fee and is not in the total.

notIncluded.label: Name reservation
notIncluded.reason: Optional. Reserving a name before you file is a separate charge and is not in the total.

notIncluded.label: Expedited filing and certified copies
notIncluded.reason: Optional. Faster processing and certified copies cost extra and are not in the total.

notIncluded.label: Local business licenses and permits
notIncluded.reason: City, county and industry licenses depend on where the business operates and what it does. None are in the total.

notIncluded.label: Federal and state income taxes
notIncluded.reason: Taxes on the LLC's or its owners' income are not part of this estimate. This page is not legal or tax advice.

content.intro: {state} charges a one-time fee to file Articles of Organization and has no annual report for LLCs. Publishing a notice of the filing can add a cost.

howItWorks.text: The Corporation Commission's fee schedule lists the regular fee for Articles of Organization and a higher fee for expedited processing.
The Commission says LLCs do not file annual reports, so there is no yearly state fee in the estimate.

A notice of the filing must be published after the Commission approves the Articles. If the statutory agent is in Maricopa or Pima county, the Commission posts it on its website. Otherwise it goes in a newspaper, which charges for it.

faq.q: Do I have to publish my {state} Articles of Organization?
faq.text: Yes. The notice is posted by the Commission for agents in Maricopa or Pima county. Elsewhere it must run in a newspaper, and that cost is not in the estimate.
